title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Explore the best of Drew University and Madison without spending a dime. From serene forest trails and historic architecture to late-night student events and art galleries, these campus and local spots offer free social and recreational opportunities for every student.

cards.title: Hike the Forest Trails
cards.subtitle: Nature trails behind the athletic fields
cards.notes: Explore 45 acres of native woodland and glacial ponds. The trails are open to the public and students for birdwatching and quiet walks through the 'Forest'.
cards.short_summary: A 45-acre natural woodland on campus featuring diverse bird species and ecological restoration sites.
cards.evidence_claim: The Drew Forest Preserve trails are open to the public and include a self-guiding nature trail around the ponds.
cards.source_title: Biodiversity and Ecological Restoration at Drew
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk; enter through the gates near the baseball outfield and close them behind you.

cards.title: Relax by the Ponds
cards.subtitle: South end of campus
cards.notes: Visit the two small ponds within the arboretum for a peaceful study break. It serves as a natural laboratory and a quiet retreat for the community.
cards.short_summary: A serene arboretum featuring two ponds that serve as a natural laboratory and a woodland retreat.
cards.evidence_claim: The arboretum and its two small ponds serve as natural laboratories and a woodland retreat with free admission.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Drew Forest Preserve trails; open during daylight hours.

cards.title: View Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: Dorothy Young Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Browse rotating exhibitions featuring professional artists and student work. The gallery hosts about six shows a year with free admission for all.
cards.short_summary: A campus art gallery presenting diverse exhibitions, including student shows and artist-in-residence projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Korn Gallery is open Tuesday through Friday, 12-4pm, and offers free admission to its exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Explore Inspiring Art at Korn Gallery
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Friday 12:00 PM - 4:00 PM during the academic year.

cards.title: Tour Historic Mead Hall
cards.subtitle: The administrative core of campus
cards.notes: Walk through this 1833 Greek Revival mansion. While it houses offices, the main hall and architecture are open for self-guided appreciation.
cards.short_summary: An iconic 19th-century Greek Revival building that serves as the symbolic heart of the university.
cards.evidence_claim: Mead Hall is a working university building with offices and meeting rooms, and its architecture is a focal point for the community.
cards.access_notes: Open during standard university business hours, typically Monday-Friday 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM.

cards.title: Join Friday Night Events
cards.subtitle: Ehinger Center (EC)
cards.notes: Attend free late-night social events every Friday starting at 8pm. Activities include games, crafts, and themed mixers for all students.
cards.short_summary: A student-led program providing free late-night social activities on Friday evenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Drew Night Life plans late night events every Friday night starting at 8pm in the Ehinger Center.
cards.access_notes: Events typically begin at 8:00 PM on Fridays in the Ehinger Center.

cards.entity_name: United Methodist Archives and History Center
cards.title: Research Global History
cards.subtitle: Across from Rose Memorial Library
cards.notes: Access one of the world's largest collections of Methodist history. The Wilson Reading Room is open to students and visitors for free research.
cards.short_summary: A major archival center housing extensive records of United Methodism and university history.
cards.evidence_claim: The materials held in The United Methodist Archives and History Center are available to anyone interested in viewing them for free.
cards.source_title: United Methodist Archives and History Center
cards.access_notes: Reading room open Monday-Friday 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM; non-Drew visitors require an appointment.

cards.title: Swim or Play Squash
cards.subtitle: Campus athletic complex
cards.notes: Use your student ID to access the 25-yard pool, indoor track, and racquetball courts. Most campus recreation services are free for students.
cards.short_summary: The primary athletic facility on campus offering a pool, fitness rooms, and various sports courts.
cards.evidence_claim: Most campus services and events, including access to the Simon Forum, are free for Drew students.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during the academic year; valid Drew ID required for entry.

cards.title: Attend Free Concerts
cards.subtitle: Music Department performances
cards.notes: Enjoy free performances by the Drew Orchestra, Jazz Ensemble, and Flute Ensemble. Most end-of-semester recitals are open to the public.
cards.short_summary: A venue for high-quality musical performances by student ensembles and faculty, often free to attend.
cards.evidence_claim: Drew University celebrates the end of the semester with musical performances that are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Drew University Announces Free Musical Performances
cards.access_notes: Concerts typically held in the evenings; check the university calendar for specific dates.

cards.title: Join Library Programs
cards.subtitle: 39 Keep Street, Madison
cards.notes: Participate in free workshops, book clubs, and film screenings just a short walk from campus. A local library card is free for residents.
cards.short_summary: The local public library offering a variety of free educational and cultural programs for the community.
cards.evidence_claim: Most programs for children, teens, and adults offered by the library are sponsored by the Friends and are free.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday 10:00 AM - 9:00 PM, Friday-Saturday 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM.

cards.title: Hang Out in the EC
cards.subtitle: Student Union building
cards.notes: Relax in the Commuter Lounge or the main student hub. It's a central spot for meeting friends, playing pool, or studying between classes.
cards.short_summary: The heart of student life on campus, featuring lounges, meeting spaces, and recreational facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The EC is a gathering place for students, staff, and faculty, offering a variety of free resources and facilities.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during the academic year; hours may vary during breaks.
